gen-gf-turret-road-fs-quicksand: Commanding and round, Turret Road draws its bowls like open parentheses. Quicksand follows in a plain sans with tall, bulb-like lowercase and terminals that stop well short of the stem, softening the heading's weight.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-actor: Bold and a bit stern, Turret Road keeps one pen-like line with no pinched joints or flared ends. And Actor adds wide, barely curled s curves, so the whole pairing feels modern and uncluttered.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-akatab: Approachable at heart, Akatab has round letters that look cupped. Turret Road stands over it with bowls drawn at stem thickness, and the two feel friendly yet firm side by side.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-alan-sans: Round forms like open parentheses, drawn in a pen-like line with no hairlines or shadows. Alan Sans holds the tails of its curves well back from the body, which makes the sans feel crisp and modern beside it.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-alef: Round, blunt and confident. Turret Road keeps its line flat and unmodulated, and Alef answers with open-ended curves throughout, a sans that stays low and tidy beneath the heading.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-alegreya-sans-sc: Parenthesis-round and boldly flat. Alegreya Sans SC brings an open, welcoming gap to its c, so a long passage under Turret Road should read in a contemporary, easygoing way.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-almarai: Those round forms, like open parentheses, are the signature of Turret Road. But Almarai keeps a sans-serif line that never swells or tapers, and the heading earns its place when it runs big and short.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-amarna: Contemporary in spirit, Amarna draws contrast-free strokes from stem to terminal. Turret Road brings its commanding round forms above, and the sans-serif text underneath keeps every small counter unclogged.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-andika: Round forms that read like open parentheses mark Turret Road out at once. Andika is the sans-serif that steps in for the reading, with thick tails and s shapes that take wide, easy turns.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-anta: Turret Road's round, parenthesis-like forms carry a pen-like line of constant weight. And Anta, a plain sans with gaping mouths on the e, gives a longer passage a wire-bent, approachable feel.
